rubric_hint.rule: 1 eligible species recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, none within 250 m
rubric_hint.basis: prompts/rubric.md v1 applied to all rings 0-1000 m and effort; a default, not a verdict

reasons.claim: 3.28 ha regeneration felling notified 2026-10-02; completed-felling overlap 0%, so not ALREADY_FELLED.
No eligible species within 250 m. The only threatened species there is Delichon urbicum (VU), a mobile bird that is not felling-relevant, so it is not eligible.

One eligible species lies beyond 250 m but within 1000 m: the VU site-bound lichen Alectoria sarmentosa. It is a single record from 2018, 848 m away, with 250 m coordinate uncertainty. Its threats include lack of continuity forest and lack of large/old trees. This gives the mechanical MEDIUM.

Two site-bound forest NT fungi are recorded within 250 m (Fomitopsis rosea and Phellinidium ferrugineofuscum, both 97 m, 2023, 10 m uncertainty). That is below the threshold of 3 and they are not eligible, so they are supporting context only.
Recording effort is adequate (220 records, 90th percentile; 21 records and 10 days within 250 m), so the near-site picture is reasonably informed.

uncertainties: The sole eligible record is old (2018), coarse (250 m uncertainty) and near the edge of the 1000 m ring. This could justify a lower priority, but I kept the mechanical MEDIUM rather than override downward.
335 records were dropped from the 1000 m ring for coordinate uncertainty, so some nearby records may be missing.
Records are not proof of occupancy of the polygon today.
not_established: Whether Alectoria sarmentosa or any other red-listed species occurs in the polygon.
The stand's age, structure or habitat value.
Anything about sensitive species hidden from public data.
That the site is safe to fell.
next_action: A reviewer should check the 2018 Alectoria sarmentosa record location and whether the stand connects to that habitat. They should also look at the stand's dead-wood and old-tree features, given the two NT fungi at 97 m.
